rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The story at a glance "My Old Home" by Lu Xun is a story about going back and finding that home exists only in memory. The narrator, educated and now urban, returns to his hometown after twenty years to move his mother and the household, and meets Runtu — the peasant boy of his childhood, the friend who taught him the countryside's secrets — now a stooped, silent father of many, broken by taxes and famine, who…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Childhood friendship (Runtu) vs adult class distance — nostalgia meets social critique.
The 'hope' ending: roads made by walking; memorise the closing metaphor.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: The 'roads' metaphor at the end: paths exist because people walk them — explain it as the essay's philosophy of change.  ·  ## The characters worth an essay **The narrator** is the story's conscience: educated, urban, and honest enough to feel the shame of his own elevation. His gesture — wanting to refuse the "Master", wanting the children to stay equals — is the story's moral action, small and insufficient and real.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The themes worth an essay **Class and its walls** — the central theme: the friendship that class destroyed and the hierarchy that both men maintain; the story is a study of how inequality insinuates itself into speech. **Memory and change** — the hometown that shrinks, the friend who ages: the theme that return is impossible because the past is not a place.…  ·  ## NEB short answers, solved **Q. Why does the narrator return to his old home? (2 marks)** A. To move his mother and the household to the city where he now lives, selling the family property in the process. The practical errand becomes an emotional audit: the visit measures the distance between the home he remembers and the one he finds. **Q. Who was Runtu in the narrator's childhood? (2 marks)** A.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. How has Runtu changed since childhood? (2 marks) — the lively boy has become a hardened, deferential poor farmer crushed by taxes and hardship.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ## NEB long answers, solved **Q. "A thick wall had grown between the narrator and Runtu." What is the wall, and how did it grow? (8 marks)** A model answer defines the wall as class distance internalised: the hierarchy of master and labourer that replaced childhood equality, expressed in the word "Master", the bowed head and the careful speech.…  ·  **‘My Old Home’ — memory vs reality (classified)** | Theme | Memory | Reality | |---|---|---| | Home | Golden childhood place | Dilapidated, dim | | Friendship | Runtu the hero of stories | Runtu the worn servant | | Class | Playmates equal | Master and servant | | Hope | New life for the young | Uncertain road ahead |

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The plot, retold with an eye on its turns The return is the story's frame: the narrator arrives in cold, grey weather to sell the family property and transport his mother — and the hometown of memory is disappointingly small, dim and unimproved. The melancholy is established before any meeting: the place itself has shrunk.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Contrast** — the story's engine: memory against reality — the quick, bright boy against the stooped, silent man; the golden moonlit watermelon field against the cold grey hometown; the children's equality against the adults' hierarchy. - **Symbolism** — the wall ("a thick barrier had been set up between us") is the story's central image: class distance as architecture.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: The core contrast: childhood friendship (Runtu the agile boy) vs adult meeting (Runtu the broken tenant, 'Master') — class barriers replace warmth; structure the answer on this contrast.  ·  Trick 2: The narrator's hope: the next generation must not be separated as they were — quote the hope line about new life.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. What does the final 'roads' metaphor mean? (2 marks) — hope creates its own path where none existed; change is made by acting.
